title: Local vs Global: Place State Where It Belongs
prompt:
Two pieces of state with very different scopes. Modal open/close is local to the consumer; the auth user is shared everywhere. Place each correctly. **Requirements:** 1. In `auth.ts`, import `create` from `zustand`. Define and export `type AuthUser = { id: number; name: string };` and `export const useAuthStore = create<{ user: AuthUser | null; setUser: (u: AuthUser | null) => void }>()((set) => ({ user: null, setUser: (u) => set({ user: u }) }));`. The auth user is global because every screen needs it. 2. In `Modal.tsx`, import `useState` from `react`. Define and export `function Modal()` that: - Uses LOCAL `useState(false)` for `open`. - Renders `` and, when `open`, `

hi

`. 3. In `Header.tsx`, import `useAuthStore` and export `function Header()` that reads `const user = useAuthStore((s) => s.user)` and renders `
{user ?

signed in: {user.name}

:

guest

}
`.
hints: Default to local `useState`. Only lift state when more than one component needs it AND they aren't naturally co-located.
Auth, theme, current user -- almost always global. Modal toggles, hover state, form drafts -- almost always local.
If you're not sure, start local; refactor to global only when you actually need it elsewhere.
